claim: The PIH protein family consists of four members in vertebrates.
source: The PIH protein family, consisting of four members, has been implicated in the assembly of different dynein subtypes, although evidence for this idea is sparse.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract and supported by the identification of four PIH proteins in zebrafish genome.

claim: Zebrafish has four PIH proteins: Pih1d1, Pih1d2, Ktu, and Twister.
source: We thus conclude that zebrafish has four PIH proteins: Pih1d1, Pih1d2, Ktu, and Twister.
evidence: Determined by BLASTp search and confirmed by checking for paralogues.

claim: Teleost fish have undergone an additional genome duplication.
source: Although teleost fish are known to have undergone an additional genome duplication (Kasahara et al., 2007), only four hits were obtained, similar to the human genome and consistent with a previous report (Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: Referenced to Kasahara et al., 2007.

claim: Domain structures of PIH proteins are well conserved among vertebrates.
source: Their domain structures are well conserved among vertebrates (Figure 1A; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B comparing zebrafish and human PIH protein domains.

claim: Transcripts of all four PIH genes were detected in ciliated organs such as Kupffer's vesicle, floor plate, otic vesicle and pronephric duct.
source: Transcripts of these four PIH genes were all detected in ciliated organs such as Kupffer's vesicle, floor plate, otic vesicle and pronephric duct (Figure 1D–G), suggesting their involvement in ciliary functions.
evidence: Demonstrated by whole-mount in situ hybridization shown in Figure 1D.

claim: pih1d1 was ubiquitously expressed in 12 hpf embryos including Kupffer's vesicle and floor plate.
source: pih1d1 was ubiquitously expressed in 12 hpf embryos (black asterisk) containing Kupffer's vesicle and floor plate (red arrowheads).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1D whole-mount in situ hybridization.

claim: ktu was expressed in brain rudiments at 32 hpf.
source: ktu was also expressed in brain rudiments at 32 hpf (black arrowhead).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1D whole-mount in situ hybridization.

claim: KTU function in brain was reported for ciliated ependymal cells in mouse.
source: In mouse, KTU function in brain was reported for ciliated ependymal cells (Matsuo et al., 2013).
evidence: Referenced to Matsuo et al., 2013.

claim: pih1d2, ktu, and twister have cilia-specific functions.
source: These results suggest that pih1d2, ktu, and twister have cilia-specific functions, while pih1d1 has ubiquitous cellular functions in addition to ciliary function.
evidence: Inferred from expression patterns shown in Figure 1D and comparison with known PIH1D1 functions.

claim: pih1d1 has ubiquitous cellular functions in addition to ciliary function.
source: These results suggest that pih1d2, ktu, and twister have cilia-specific functions, while pih1d1 has ubiquitous cellular functions in addition to ciliary function.
evidence: Inferred from ubiquitous expression pattern and known functions of PIH1D1.

claim: DNAAFs including PIH proteins are known to be localized to the cytoplasm.
source: Since DNAAFs including PIH proteins are known to be localized to the cytoplasm (Kobayashi and Takeda, 2012), we examined the subcellular localizations of zebrafish PIH proteins by immunoblot analysis, using specific polyclonal antibodies made in this study.
evidence: Referenced to Kobayashi and Takeda, 2012.

claim: All zebrafish PIH proteins were detected in both testis lysate and sperm lysate.
source: All PIH proteins were detected in both testis lysate and sperm lysate.
evidence: Shown by immunoblot analysis in Figure 1C.

claim: Zebrafish PIH proteins are specifically present in the cytoplasm, but not in the flagellar compartment.
source: However, when spermatozoa were fractionated into sperm heads and flagella, PIH proteins were detected only in the sperm head fraction, indicating that like other DNAAFs, zebrafish PIH proteins are indeed specifically present in the cytoplasm, but not in the flagellar compartment (Figure 1C; asterisks).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoblot analysis of fractionated sperm shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Homozygous mutants of each PIH gene were viable.
source: Since homozygous mutants of each PIH gene were viable, we established homozygous mutant lines.
evidence: Observed during the generation and maintenance of mutant lines.

claim: All mutations resulted in a null of each PIH protein.
source: Immunoblot analysis confirmed that all mutations resulted in a null of each PIH protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Shown by immunoblot analysis in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: In pih1d1-/-, spermatozoa showed a slight reduction of beating frequency.
source: In pih1d1-/-, spermatozoa showed a slight reduction of beating frequency (Figure 2G), and propagation of flagellar bending was disturbed, as slopes of shear angle curves changed between traces (Figure 2B'; asterisk).
evidence: Measured from high-speed camera recordings and shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2B'.

claim: In pih1d1-/-, propagation of flagellar bending was disturbed.
source: In pih1d1-/-, spermatozoa showed a slight reduction of beating frequency (Figure 2G), and propagation of flagellar bending was disturbed, as slopes of shear angle curves changed between traces (Figure 2B'; asterisk).
evidence: Shown by shear angle analysis in Figure 2B'.

claim: In twister-/-, almost all spermatozoa were immotile.
source: In twister-/-, almost all spermatozoa were immotile, but a few were found to be motile with decreased beating frequencies and severely disturbed waveforms (Figure 2E).
evidence: Observed by high-speed camera and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: In pih1d2-/- and ktu-/-, a significant difference was not observed in either beating frequencies or waveforms.
source: In pih1d2-/- and ktu-/-, a significant difference was not observed in either beating frequencies or waveforms (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2C,D from high-speed camera analysis.

claim: Double mutant pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- spermatozoa exhibited abnormal waveforms; motile in the proximal half, while immotile in the distal half.
source: Double mutant spermatozoa exhibited abnormal waveforms; motile in the proximal half, while immotile in the distal half (Figure 2F).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2F from high-speed camera analysis.

claim: In pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- proximal region, beating frequency was about twice as high as that of wild type.
source: In the proximal region, beating frequency was about twice as high as that of wild type (Figure 2G).
evidence: Measured from kymographs and shown in Figure 2G.

claim: The increased beating frequency in pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- could be caused by the reduction of sliding distance of DMTs, rather than the change of the sliding velocity of DMTs.
source: This could be caused by the reduction of sliding distance of DMTs, rather than the change of the sliding velocity of DMTs, because the slopes of shear angle curves was decreased (Figure 2F'; dotted line), indicating that the bending of the proximal flagella was smaller than that of wild type.
evidence: Inferred from shear angle analysis shown in Figure 2F'.

claim: No significant differences in sperm flagella length were found between wild type and PIH gene mutants.
source: We also analyzed the length of sperm flagella, but did not find any significant differences between wild type and PIH gene mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Measured by immunofluorescent staining and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In all PIH gene mutants, the ratios of motile (locomotive) spermatozoa were significantly decreased.
source: In all mutants, the ratios of motile (locomotive) spermatozoa were significantly decreased, and no sperm in twister-/- showed significant locomotion (Figure 2H).
evidence: Measured by CASA and shown in Figure 2H.

claim: No sperm in twister-/- showed significant locomotion.
source: In all mutants, the ratios of motile (locomotive) spermatozoa were significantly decreased, and no sperm in twister-/- showed significant locomotion (Figure 2H).
evidence: Measured by CASA and shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Swimming velocity did not change in pih1d1-/-, pih1d2-/-, and ktu-/- motile spermatozoa.
source: For motile spermatozoa, swimming velocity did not change in pih1d1-/-, pih1d2-/-, and ktu-/-, but significantly decreased in pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- (Figure 2I).
evidence: Measured by CASA and shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Swimming velocity significantly decreased in pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- motile spermatozoa.
source: For motile spermatozoa, swimming velocity did not change in pih1d1-/-, pih1d2-/-, and ktu-/-, but significantly decreased in pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- (Figure 2I).
evidence: Measured by CASA and shown in Figure 2I.

claim: The beating frequencies of sperm heads were decreased in pih1d1-/-, but increased in pih1d2-/-;ktu-/-.
source: The beating frequencies of sperm heads were decreased in pih1d1-/-, but increased in pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- (Figure 2J), which is consistent with Figure 2G.
evidence: Measured by CASA and shown in Figure 2J.

claim: The axoneme of zebrafish sperm had the characteristic 9 + 2 arrangement of DMTs surrounding central-pair microtubules.
source: The axoneme of zebrafish sperm had the characteristic 9 + 2 arrangement of DMTs surrounding central-pair microtubules (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Observed by cryo-ET and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Subtomographic averaging was applied using the 96 nm repeat of DMTs assuming nine-fold rotational symmetry of the axoneme.
source: To analyze the structure of DMTs in more detail, subtomographic averaging was applied using the 96 nm repeat of DMTs assuming nine-fold rotational symmetry of the axoneme, since we did not detect any obvious heterogeneity of nine DMTs in zebrafish sperm unlike Chlamydomonas flagella and sea urchin sperm (Hoops and Witman, 1983; Bui et al., 2012; Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: Methodological approach based on structural observations and comparison with other organisms.

claim: The averaged structure of zebrafish DMT exhibited overall similarity to that of other organisms.
source: The averaged structure of zebrafish DMT exhibited overall similarity to that of other organisms (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: Shown by comparison of structures in Figure 3C,D.

claim: Zebrafish axoneme does not have OAD α-HCs.
source: Compared with Chlamydomonas, zebrafish axoneme does not have OAD α-HCs, but has longer RS3 (Figure 3A,D).
evidence: Observed by comparing cryo-ET structures in Figure 3A,D.

claim: Zebrafish axoneme has longer RS3 compared with Chlamydomonas.
source: Compared with Chlamydomonas, zebrafish axoneme does not have OAD α-HCs, but has longer RS3 (Figure 3A,D).
evidence: Observed by comparing cryo-ET structures in Figure 3A,D.

claim: A linker between N-DRC and OAD is not observed in the zebrafish axoneme unlike Chlamydomonas.
source: A linker between N-DRC and OAD is not observed in the zebrafish axoneme unlike Chlamydomonas (Figure 3D; red arrowhead).
evidence: Observed by comparing cryo-ET structures in Figure 3D.

claim: The features of zebrafish axoneme (no OAD α-HCs, longer RS3, no N-DRC-OAD linker) are also found in human respiratory cilia.
source: These features of the zebrafish axoneme are also found in human respiratory cilia (Figure 3C; Lin et al., 2014).
evidence: Comparison with published structure referenced to Lin et al., 2014.

claim: The same features were also reported in mouse respiratory cilia and found in sea urchin spermatozoa, indicating that these features are common among metazoans.
source: The same features were also reported in mouse respiratory cilia (Ueno et al., 2012) and found in sea urchin spermatozoa (Lin et al., 2012), indicating that these features are common among metazoans.
evidence: Referenced to Ueno et al., 2012 and Lin et al., 2012.

claim: IAD c was missing in pih1d1-/-.
source: IAD c was missing in pih1d1-/- (Figure 3F; Video 4), while no significant difference was observed in pih1d2-/- (Figure 3G; Video 5).
evidence: Observed by cryo-ET and shown in Figure 3F.

claim: No significant difference was observed in pih1d2-/- axoneme structure.
source: IAD c was missing in pih1d1-/- (Figure 3F; Video 4), while no significant difference was observed in pih1d2-/- (Figure 3G; Video 5).
evidence: Observed by cryo-ET and shown in Figure 3G.

claim: In ktu-/-, smaller IAD c density was observed, suggesting that IAD c is partially missing in ktu-/- spermatozoa.
source: In ktu-/-, smaller IAD c density was observed, suggesting that IAD c is partially missing in ktu-/- spermatozoa (Figure 3H; Video 6).
evidence: Observed by cryo-ET and shown in Figure 3H.

claim: In twister-/-, OADs and IAD c were missing and smaller IAD g and d were observed.
source: In twister-/-, reflecting severe motility defects, OADs and IAD c were missing and smaller IAD g and d were observed (Figure 3I; Video 7).
evidence: Observed by cryo-ET and shown in Figure 3I.

claim: In pih1d2-/-;ktu-/-, four axonemes had OADs but five lacked OADs out of nine tomograms.
source: We noticed that out of nine tomograms of axonemes, four axonemes had OADs but five lacked OADs.
evidence: Observed during cryo-ET analysis of pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- axonemes.

claim: The +OAD class of pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- possessed a full set of axonemal dyneins, except for a smaller IAD c.
source: The +OAD class possessed a full set of axonemal dyneins, except for a smaller IAD c, like the ktu-/- axoneme (Figure 3J; Video 8).
evidence: Observed by cryo-ET and shown in Figure 3J.

claim: The -OAD class of pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- lost not only OADs, but also IAD b, c, and e.
source: By contrast, the -OAD class lost not only OADs, but also IAD b, c, and e (Figure 3K; Video 9).
evidence: Observed by cryo-ET and shown in Figure 3K.

claim: The –OAD class showed faint densities of IAD b, c, and e in the subtomographic slice, suggesting that these IADs were retained partially.
source: However, note that the –OAD class showed faint densities of these IADs in the subtomographic slice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), which suggests that IAD b, c, and e were retained partially in the –OAD class axonemes.
evidence: Observed in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: No significant defect was observed in other DMT structures, such as RSs, in all mutants examined.
source: Although we found structural defects of axonemal dyneins, no significant defect was observed in other DMT structures, such as RSs, in all mutants we examined.
evidence: Observed by cryo-ET analysis of all mutants.

claim: Dnah8 and Dnai1 were missing from the axoneme of twister-/-.
source: Consistent with the above structural analysis, Dnah8 and Dnai1 were missing from the axoneme of twister-/- (Figure 4A; asterisks).
evidence: Shown by immunoblot analysis in Figure 4A.

claim: In pih1d2-/-;ktu-/-, the amount of Dnah8 and Dnai1 was decreased.
source: In pih1d2-/-;ktu-/-, the amount of Dnah8 and Dnai1 was decreased, possibly reflecting the presence of the two types of DMT structures (+OAD and -OAD).
evidence: Shown by immunoblot analysis in Figure 4A and correlated with structural findings.

claim: Dnah2 was not affected in any mutants.
source: Dnah2 was not affected in any mutants, and so was the case of IAD f in the structural analysis.
evidence: Shown by immunoblot analysis in Figure 4A.

claim: IAD f was not affected in any mutants in the structural analysis.
source: Dnah2 was not affected in any mutants, and so was the case of IAD f in the structural analysis.
evidence: Observed by cryo-ET analysis.

claim: Dnali1 was slightly decreased in pih1d1-/-, ktu-/-, and pih1d2-/-;ktu-/-.
source: Dnali1 was slightly decreased in pih1d1-/-, ktu-/-, and pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- (Figure 4A; filled circles), confirming the loss of IAD c (one of three IADs containing p28 in Chlamydomonas) in these mutants.
evidence: Shown by immunoblot analysis in Figure 4A.

claim: In twister-/-, the amount of Dnali1 was strongly reduced.
source: In twister-/-, the structural analysis revealed the loss of IAD c and d (two of three IADs containing p28), and the amount of Dnali1 was strongly reduced.
evidence: Shown by immunoblot analysis in Figure 4A and correlated with structural findings.

claim: Shifted bands of Dnai1 were observed in pih1d1-/- and pih1d2-/-, indicating abnormal construction of OADs in these mutants.
source: Interestingly, shifted bands of Dnai1 were observed in pih1d1-/- and pih1d2-/- (Figure 4A; open circles), indicating abnormal construction of OADs in these mutants.
evidence: Shown by immunoblot analysis in Figure 4A.

claim: The structure of OADs in pih1d1-/- and pih1d2-/- appeared normal as far as the structural analysis showed at the current resolution.
source: However, the structure of OADs in these mutants appeared normal as far as our structural analysis showed at the current resolution.
evidence: Observed by cryo-ET analysis.

claim: All biochemical results are largely consistent with the structural data.
source: Taken together, all biochemical results are largely consistent with our structural data.
evidence: Comparison of immunoblot and cryo-ET results.

claim: All PIH proteins are responsible for the assembly of specific subtypes of axonemal dyneins.
source: From these results, we conclude that all PIH proteins are responsible for the assembly of specific subtypes of axonemal dyneins.
evidence: Concluded from combined structural and biochemical analyses of all PIH mutants.

claim: All vertebrate PIH proteins (not only Ktu and Twister, but also Pih1d1 and Pih1d2) are DNAAFs.
source: Together with their specific cytoplasmic localizations, we identified all vertebrate PIH proteins (not only Ktu and Twister, but also Pih1d1 and Pih1d2) as DNAAFs.
evidence: Concluded from cytoplasmic localization and effects on dynein assembly.

claim: Abnormal sperm motility observed in pih1d1-/-, twister-/- and pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- can be explained by the loss of specific subtypes of axonemal dyneins.
source: Abnormal sperm motility observed in pih1d1-/-, twister-/- and pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- can be explained by the loss of specific subtypes of axonemal dyneins.
evidence: Correlation between structural defects and motility phenotypes.

claim: Spermatozoa of pih1d2-/- and ktu-/- appeared to have normal motility, although the structural or biochemical analyses revealed abnormal axonemal dyneins in these mutants.
source: On the other hand, spermatozoa of pih1d2-/- and ktu-/- appeared to have normal motility, although the structural or biochemical analyses revealed abnormal axonemal dyneins in these mutants.
evidence: Comparison of motility and structural/biochemical data.

claim: The defects of axonemal dyneins in pih1d2-/- or ktu-/- spermatozoa are so subtle that other normal axonemal dyneins can compensate their loss of function.
source: A likely explanation for this discrepancy is that the defects of axonemal dyneins in pih1d2-/- or ktu-/- spermatozoa are so subtle that other normal axonemal dyneins can compensate their loss of function.
evidence: Proposed explanation for the discrepancy between structural defects and normal motility.

claim: The affected axonemal dyneins were different between pih1d2-/- (OAD Dnai1) and ktu-/- (IAD c), which indicates distinct functions of Pih1d2 and Ktu.
source: However, it is worth noting that the affected axonemal dyneins were different between pih1d2-/- (OAD Dnai1) and ktu-/- (IAD c), which indicates distinct functions of Pih1d2 and Ktu, although functional compensation of these two genes was also revealed by pih1d2-/-;ktu-/-.
evidence: Comparison of biochemical and structural defects between mutants.

claim: Functional compensation of Pih1d2 and Ktu was revealed by pih1d2-/-;ktu-/-.
source: However, it is worth noting that the affected axonemal dyneins were different between pih1d2-/- (OAD Dnai1) and ktu-/- (IAD c), which indicates distinct functions of Pih1d2 and Ktu, although functional compensation of these two genes was also revealed by pih1d2-/-;ktu-/-.
evidence: Observed by comparing single and double mutant phenotypes.

claim: In pih1d2-/-;ktu-/-, Dnah8 was consistently absent in the distal region, while it remained in the proximal.
source: However, in pih1d2-/-;ktu-/-, Dnah8 was consistently absent in the distal region, while it remained in the proximal (Figure 4B; white arrowhead).
evidence: Shown by immunofluorescence microscopy in Figure 4B.

claim: The +OAD class structure was localized in the proximal region of pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- axoneme, while the -OAD class was in the distal.
source: Thus, the +OAD class structure was localized in the proximal region, while the -OAD class was in the distal.
evidence: Concluded from Dnah8 immunofluorescence distribution.

claim: In pih1d1-/-, pih1d2-/-, and ktu-/- spermatozoa, Dnah8 was normally distributed along the entire length of their flagella.
source: Consistent with our structural analysis, in pih1d1-/-, pih1d2-/-, and ktu-/- spermatozoa, Dnah8 was normally distributed along the entire length of their flagella, while twister-/- spermatozoa completely lost Dnah8.
evidence: Shown by immunofluorescence microscopy in Figure 4B.

claim: twister-/- spermatozoa completely lost Dnah8.
source: Consistent with our structural analysis, in pih1d1-/-, pih1d2-/-, and ktu-/- spermatozoa, Dnah8 was normally distributed along the entire length of their flagella, while twister-/- spermatozoa completely lost Dnah8.
evidence: Shown by immunofluorescence microscopy in Figure 4B.

claim: The DMT structure of a proximal subtomogram of pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- possessed OADs and the densities of all IADs, consistent with the structure of +OAD class.
source: Although the obtained subtomograms are noisy due to a smaller number of averaged particles, the DMT structure of a proximal subtomogram possessed OADs and the densities of all IADs, consistent with the structure of +OAD class (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,D).
evidence: Shown by cryo-ET analysis in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,D.

claim: The DMT structure of a distal subtomogram of pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- lost OADs, IAD b, c, and e, which corresponds to -OAD class.
source: On the other hand, the DMT structure of a distal subtomogram lost OADs, IAD b, c, and e, which corresponds to -OAD class (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,E).
evidence: Shown by cryo-ET analysis in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,E.

claim: The distribution of not only OADs but also IADs is different between the proximal and distal regions in pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- spermatozoa.
source: Therefore, the distribution of not only OADs but also IADs is different between the proximal and distal regions in pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- spermatozoa.
evidence: Concluded from direct cryo-ET observation of proximal and distal regions.

claim: Organ-specific compositions of OAD HCs were reported between sperm flagella and respiratory cilia in humans.
source: In humans, organ-specific compositions of OAD HCs were reported between sperm flagella and respiratory cilia (Figure 7E; Fliegauf et al., 2005; Dougherty et al., 2016), and mouse Pih1d3 was reported as a testis-specific gene (Dong et al., 2014).
evidence: Referenced to Fliegauf et al., 2005 and Dougherty et al., 2016.

claim: Mouse Pih1d3 was reported as a testis-specific gene.
source: In humans, organ-specific compositions of OAD HCs were reported between sperm flagella and respiratory cilia (Figure 7E; Fliegauf et al., 2005; Dougherty et al., 2016), and mouse Pih1d3 was reported as a testis-specific gene (Dong et al., 2014).
evidence: Referenced to Dong et al., 2014.

claim: Kupffer's vesicle is orthologous to the mammalian embryonic node.
source: To assess organ-specific functions of zebrafish PIH proteins, we focused on a second ciliated organ, Kupffer's vesicle, which is orthologous to the mammalian embryonic node.
evidence: Established knowledge about Kupffer's vesicle.

claim: In Kupffer's vesicle, epithelial cells project mono-cilia that have rotational motility to produce leftward fluid flow in the organ.
source: In Kupffer's vesicle, epithelial cells project mono-cilia that have rotational motility to produce leftward fluid flow in the organ (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5A,B and established knowledge.

claim: Leftward flow in Kupffer's vesicle is required for the determination of visceral asymmetry.
source: Like in the mouse node, this leftward flow is required for the determination of visceral asymmetry, and thus defects of Kupffer's vesicle cilia cause abnormal left-right patterning of the fish (Essner et al., 2005).
evidence: Referenced to Essner et al., 2005.

claim: Defects of Kupffer's vesicle cilia cause abnormal left-right patterning of the fish.
source: Like in the mouse node, this leftward flow is required for the determination of visceral asymmetry, and thus defects of Kupffer's vesicle cilia cause abnormal left-right patterning of the fish (Essner et al., 2005).
evidence: Referenced to Essner et al., 2005.

claim: Mutations of each PIH gene caused abnormal motility of Kupffer's vesicle cilia.
source: Mutations of each PIH gene caused abnormal motility of Kupffer's vesicle cilia.
evidence: Observed by high-speed camera analysis.

claim: In pih1d1-/-, rotational frequencies of Kupffer's vesicle cilia were significantly reduced, but almost all cilia were motile and the ratio of heart-looping reversal was not largely affected.
source: In pih1d1-/-, rotational frequencies of cilia were significantly reduced, but almost all cilia were motile and the ratio of heart-looping reversal was not largely affected.
evidence: Shown in Figure 5D,E,F from high-speed camera analysis and heart looping observations.

claim: In twister-/- and pih1d2-/-;ktu-/-, all Kupffer's vesicle cilia were immotile, leading to complete randomization of their left-right patterning.
source: By contrast, in twister-/- and pih1d2-/-;ktu-/-, all cilia were immotile, leading to complete randomization of their left-right patterning.
evidence: Shown in Figure 5D,F from high-speed camera analysis and heart looping observations.

claim: In pih1d2-/- and ktu-/-, the proportions of rotating class cilia were decreased to ~40% and~15%, respectively, with reduced rotational frequencies, resulting in significant levels of heart-looping defects.
source: In pih1d2-/- and ktu-/-, the proportions of rotating class cilia were decreased to ~40% and~15%, respectively, with reduced rotational frequencies, resulting in significant levels of heart-looping defects (Figure 5D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5D,E,F from high-speed camera analysis and heart looping observations.

claim: All PIH genes of zebrafish are essential for normal motility of both sperm flagella and Kupffer's vesicle cilia.
source: Together with sperm analyses, we conclude that all PIH genes of zebrafish are essential for normal motility of both sperm flagella and Kupffer's vesicle cilia.
evidence: Concluded from combined analyses of sperm and Kupffer's vesicle cilia.

claim: In pih1d2-/- and ktu-/-, only Kupffer's vesicle cilia showed motility defects, while sperm flagella beat normally, indicating that Pih1d2 and Ktu have organ-specific functions.
source: Intriguingly, however, in pih1d2-/- and ktu-/-, only Kupffer's vesicle cilia showed motility defects, while sperm flagella beat normally, indicating that Pih1d2 and Ktu have organ-specific functions.
evidence: Comparison of phenotypes between sperm and Kupffer's vesicle cilia.

claim: The organ-specific phenotypes of PIH mutants could reflect organ-specific compositions of axonemal dyneins.
source: The organ-specific phenotypes of PIH mutants could reflect organ-specific compositions of axonemal dyneins.
evidence: Proposed explanation for organ-specific phenotypes.

claim: Zebrafish have three OAD β-HC genes: dnah9, dnah9l, and dnah11.
source: Zebrafish have three OAD β-HC genes: dnah9, dnah9l, and dnah11, and two OAD γ-HC genes: dnah5 and dnah8.
evidence: Identified from zebrafish genome.

claim: Zebrafish have two OAD γ-HC genes: dnah5 and dnah8.
source: Zebrafish have three OAD β-HC genes: dnah9, dnah9l, and dnah11, and two OAD γ-HC genes: dnah5 and dnah8.
evidence: Identified from zebrafish genome.

claim: dnah2 is an IAD f β-HC gene.
source: As for IAD, dnah2 is an IAD f β-HC gene, and dnah3 and dnah7l are other IAD HC genes.
evidence: Based on gene correspondence analysis.

claim: dnah3 and dnah7l are other IAD HC genes.
source: As for IAD, dnah2 is an IAD f β-HC gene, and dnah3 and dnah7l are other IAD HC genes.
evidence: Based on gene correspondence analysis.

claim: Zebrafish embryos and testes showed distinct expression patterns of DNAH genes.
source: Zebrafish embryos and testes showed distinct expression patterns of DNAH genes (Figure 6A).
evidence: Shown by whole-mount in situ hybridization in Figure 6A.

claim: dnah11 expression was specifically detected in Kupffer's vesicle when comparing Kupffer's vesicle and testis.
source: When comparing Kupffer's vesicle and testis, dnah11 expression was specifically detected in Kupffer's vesicle, while dnah8 and dnah3 were specifically detected in testis (Figure 6B).
evidence: Shown by whole-mount in situ hybridization in Figure 6A,B.

claim: dnah8 and dnah3 were specifically detected in testis when comparing Kupffer's vesicle and testis.
source: When comparing Kupffer's vesicle and testis, dnah11 expression was specifically detected in Kupffer's vesicle, while dnah8 and dnah3 were specifically detected in testis (Figure 6B).
evidence: Shown by whole-mount in situ hybridization in Figure 6A,B.

claim: dnah9l and dnah8 were detected only in the otic vesicle and the pronephric duct, respectively, at the embryonic stages.
source: At the embryonic stages, dnah9l and dnah8 were detected only in the otic vesicle and the pronephric duct, respectively, which also suggested specific combinations of DNAH genes in these organs.
evidence: Shown by whole-mount in situ hybridization in Figure 6A.

claim: Components of axonemal dyneins are organ-specific.
source: These results indicate that components of axonemal dyneins are indeed organ-specific.
evidence: Concluded from differential DNAH gene expression patterns.

claim: Kupffer's vesicle and floor plate showed the same expression patterns of DNAH genes.
source: Intriguingly, however, Kupffer's vesicle and floor plate, whose cilia exhibit similar rotational motility (Kramer-Zucker et al., 2005), showed the same expression patterns of DNAH genes.
evidence: Observed by whole-mount in situ hybridization and referenced to Kramer-Zucker et al., 2005.

claim: The same transcriptional regulation is likely required in Kupffer's vesicle and floor plate to construct similar types of cilia.
source: It is likely that the same transcriptional regulation is required in Kupffer's vesicle and floor plate to construct similar types of cilia.
evidence: Inferred from similar DNAH expression patterns and similar ciliary motility.

claim: All vertebrate PIH proteins are differently required for cilia/flagella motions and the assembly of axonemal dyneins.
source: Our data demonstrate that all vertebrate PIH proteins are differently required for cilia/flagella motions and the assembly of axonemal dyneins, assigning specific dynein subtypes to each PIH protein.
evidence: Concluded from systematic analysis of all PIH mutants.

claim: This is the first report that shows all vertebrate PIH proteins as DNAAFs.
source: This is the first report that shows all vertebrate PIH proteins as DNAAFs, assigning their functions to specific types of axonemal dyneins and to cilia/flagella motions.
evidence: Stated as a novel finding of the study.

claim: The data provide evidence for the hypothesis that the cytoplasmic assembly of different dynein subtypes is mediated by distinct PIH proteins.
source: Our data provide evidence for the above-mentioned hypothesis that the cytoplasmic assembly of different dynein subtypes is mediated by distinct PIH proteins.
evidence: Concluded from the systematic analysis showing each PIH protein affects different dynein subtypes.

claim: Pih1d1 is required for the assembly of OAD (Dnai1 construction) and IAD c.
source: Our cryo-ET and biochemical analyses revealed that the PIH proteins are required for the assemblies of specific subsets of axonemal dyneins (Figure 7C): Pih1d1 for OAD (Dnai1 construction) and IAD c; Pih1d2 and Ktu for OAD, IAD b, c, and e; and Twister for OAD, IAD c, g, and d.
evidence: Concluded from cryo-ET and biochemical analyses shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Pih1d2 and Ktu are required for the assembly of OAD, IAD b, c, and e.
source: Our cryo-ET and biochemical analyses revealed that the PIH proteins are required for the assemblies of specific subsets of axonemal dyneins (Figure 7C): Pih1d1 for OAD (Dnai1 construction) and IAD c; Pih1d2 and Ktu for OAD, IAD b, c, and e; and Twister for OAD, IAD c, g, and d.
evidence: Concluded from cryo-ET and biochemical analyses shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Twister is required for the assembly of OAD, IAD c, g, and d.
source: Our cryo-ET and biochemical analyses revealed that the PIH proteins are required for the assemblies of specific subsets of axonemal dyneins (Figure 7C): Pih1d1 for OAD (Dnai1 construction) and IAD c; Pih1d2 and Ktu for OAD, IAD b, c, and e; and Twister for OAD, IAD c, g, and d.
evidence: Concluded from cryo-ET and biochemical analyses shown in Figure 7C.

claim: In Chlamydomonas, the mutation of KTU/PF13 affected the assembly of OAD and IAD c.
source: In Chlamydomonas, the mutation of KTU/PF13 affected the assembly of OAD and IAD c, while the mutation of MOT48 affected the assembly of OAD, IAD b, c, d, and e (Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: Referenced to Yamamoto et al., 2010.

claim: In Chlamydomonas, the mutation of MOT48 affected the assembly of OAD, IAD b, c, d, and e.
source: In Chlamydomonas, the mutation of KTU/PF13 affected the assembly of OAD and IAD c, while the mutation of MOT48 affected the assembly of OAD, IAD b, c, d, and e (Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: Referenced to Yamamoto et al., 2010.

claim: OAD and IAD c are most sensitive to the mutations of various PIH genes in both zebrafish and Chlamydomonas.
source: Remarkably, OAD and IAD c are most sensitive to the mutations of various PIH genes in both zebrafish and Chlamydomonas.
evidence: Observed from comparison of PIH mutant phenotypes in both organisms.

claim: The assembly of OAD proceeds in a stepwise manner mediated by different PIH proteins.
source: Consistent with this, Dong et al. (2014) suggested that the assembly of OAD proceeds in a stepwise manner mediated by different PIH proteins.
evidence: Referenced to Dong et al., 2014.

claim: IAD a or f were not affected in any PIH gene mutants.
source: In our research, IAD a or f were not affected in any PIH gene mutants (Figure 7C), which was essentially the same as in Chlamydomonas mutants of KTU/PF13 and MOT48.
evidence: Observed from cryo-ET analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: IAD a or f may be assembled independently of PIH proteins or multiple PIH proteins redundantly participate in their assembly.
source: This suggests that these axonemal dyneins are assembled independently of PIH proteins. Alternatively, multiple PIH proteins redundantly participate in their assembly.
evidence: Proposed explanations for the lack of IAD a or f defects.

claim: A defect of DYX1C1 affects the normal assembly of all types of IADs in Chlamydomonas.
source: IAD a or f may not be constructed automatically, because a defect of DYX1C1 (a known DNAAF other than PIH family proteins; Tarkar et al., 2013) affects the normal assembly of all types of IADs in Chlamydomonas (Yamamoto et al., 2017).
evidence: Referenced to Tarkar et al., 2013 and Yamamoto et al., 2017.

claim: Zebrafish pih1d1-/- mutants were viable and exhibited only ciliary defects as far as observed.
source: Zebrafish pih1d1-/- mutants were viable and exhibited only ciliary defects as far as we observed.
evidence: Observed during phenotypic analysis of mutants.

claim: Pih1d1 could be mostly redundant in cellular functions.
source: Thus, Pih1d1 could be mostly redundant in cellular functions.
evidence: Inferred from viability and lack of non-ciliary phenotypes.

claim: Yeast PIH1-deletion cells were viable.
source: In fact, yeast PIH1-deletion cells were also reported to be viable (Gonzales et al., 2005), like zebrafish pih1d1-/-.
evidence: Referenced to Gonzales et al., 2005.

claim: Accumulated knowledge about DNAAFs has suggested the involvement of R2TP-like complex in the process of axonemal dynein assembly.
source: Accumulated knowledge about DNAAFs has suggested the involvement of R2TP-like complex in the process of axonemal dynein assembly (Li et al., 2017).
evidence: Referenced to Li et al., 2017.

claim: The identification of Pih1d1 as a novel DNAAF strongly supports the idea of R2TP-like complex involvement in axonemal dynein assembly.
source: We identified Pih1d1 as a novel DNAAF, which strongly support this idea.
evidence: Inferred from the finding that Pih1d1 is a DNAAF and known to be part of R2TP complex.

claim: KTU and PIH1D3 are suggested to participate in R2TP-like complexes.
source: Since KTU and PIH1D3 are also suggested to participate in R2TP-like complexes (Tarkar et al., 2013; Olcese et al., 2017), each of PIH proteins may serve as a component of R2TP-like complexes.
evidence: Referenced to Tarkar et al., 2013 and Olcese et al., 2017.

claim: Each of PIH proteins may serve as a component of R2TP-like complexes.
source: Since KTU and PIH1D3 are also suggested to participate in R2TP-like complexes (Tarkar et al., 2013; Olcese et al., 2017), each of PIH proteins may serve as a component of R2TP-like complexes.
evidence: Inferred from the involvement of multiple PIH proteins in R2TP-like complexes.

claim: It was surprising that the spermatozoa of zebrafish ktu-/- showed normal motility.
source: It was surprising that the spermatozoa of zebrafish ktu-/- showed normal motility, since abnormal sperm motility was reported in both human KTU/DNAAF2-/- patients and medaka ktu mutants (Omran et al., 2008).
evidence: Comparison with human and medaka phenotypes referenced to Omran et al., 2008.

claim: Abnormal sperm motility was reported in both human KTU/DNAAF2-/- patients and medaka ktu mutants.
source: It was surprising that the spermatozoa of zebrafish ktu-/- showed normal motility, since abnormal sperm motility was reported in both human KTU/DNAAF2-/- patients and medaka ktu mutants (Omran et al., 2008).
evidence: Referenced to Omran et al., 2008.

claim: The function of Ktu and other PIH proteins in zebrafish could have diverged during evolution.
source: This suggests that the function of Ktu and other PIH proteins in zebrafish could have diverged during evolution.
evidence: Inferred from differences in phenotypes between zebrafish and other organisms.

claim: Double mutants of pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- showed phenotypes similar to those of the medaka ktu mutant in terms of complete loss of ciliary motility in Kupffer's vesicle and the expansion of pronephric ducts.
source: Intriguingly, double mutants of pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- showed phenotypes similar to those of the medaka ktu mutant, in terms of complete loss of ciliary motility in Kupffer's vesicle (Figure 5D) and the expansion of pronephric ducts (Figure 7—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Comparison with medaka phenotypes shown in Figure 5D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The waveform of pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- spermatozoa highly resembles that of medaka ktu mutant spermatozoa.
source: Furthermore, the waveform of pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- spermatozoa highly resembles that of medaka ktu mutant spermatozoa (bends do not propagate to the tip of the sperm tail; Omran et al., 2008).
evidence: Comparison with medaka phenotypes referenced to Omran et al., 2008.

claim: The function of medaka Ktu is partially shared by Ktu and Pih1d2 in zebrafish.
source: The function of medaka Ktu is thus partially shared by Ktu and Pih1d2 in zebrafish.
evidence: Inferred from the similarity of double mutant phenotype to medaka single mutant.

claim: Functional divergence of PIH proteins was reported in human and mouse.
source: Such functional divergence of PIH proteins was also reported in human and mouse; human PIH1D3 has functions in various ciliated organs (Paff et al., 2017; Olcese et al., 2017), while mouse Pih1d3 is a testis-specific gene (Dong et al., 2014).
evidence: Referenced to Paff et al., 2017; Olcese et al., 2017; and Dong et al., 2014.

claim: Human PIH1D3 has functions in various ciliated organs.
source: Such functional divergence of PIH proteins was also reported in human and mouse; human PIH1D3 has functions in various ciliated organs (Paff et al., 2017; Olcese et al., 2017), while mouse Pih1d3 is a testis-specific gene (Dong et al., 2014).
evidence: Referenced to Paff et al., 2017 and Olcese et al., 2017.

claim: Twister2 (paralogue of mouse Pih1d3) is expressed in various ciliary organs including testis in mice but is not able to rescue the loss of Pih1d3 in testis.
source: Twister2 (paralogue of mouse Pih1d3) is expressed in various ciliary organs including testis in mice but is not able to rescue the loss of Pih1d3 in testis.
evidence: Stated as known information about mouse Twister2.

claim: PIH proteins tend to be functionally diverse and sometimes interchangeable, even though they stay in the category of DNAAFs.
source: Therefore, PIH proteins tend to be functionally diverse and sometimes interchangeable, even though they stay in the category of DNAAFs.
evidence: Concluded from examples of functional divergence and compensation among PIH proteins.

claim: One possible explanation for the distal-specific loss of dyneins in pih1d2-/-;ktu-/- is that the lack of both PIH1d2 and Ktu causes decreased efficiency of axonemal dynein assembly, leading to a shortage of dyneins to be loaded in the distal axoneme.
source: One possible explanation for this phenotype is that the lack of both PIH1d2 and Ktu causes decreased efficiency of axonemal dynein assembly, leading to a shortage of dyneins to be loaded in the distal axoneme.
evidence: Proposed explanation for the proximal-distal difference in dynein distribution.

claim: The axoneme is known to continue elongating by adding flagellar components to its distal end during ciliogenesis.
source: Actually, the axoneme is known to continue elongating by adding flagellar components to its distal end during ciliogenesis (Johnson and Rosenbaum, 1992), and in mature spermatozoa, the transport of flagellar components is highly improbable, because IFT components disappear as spermatozoa mature (San Agustin et al., 2015).
evidence: Referenced to Johnson and Rosenbaum, 1992.

claim: In mature spermatozoa, the transport of flagellar components is highly improbable, because IFT components disappear as spermatozoa mature.
source: Actually, the axoneme is known to continue elongating by adding flagellar components to its distal end during ciliogenesis (Johnson and Rosenbaum, 1992), and in mature spermatozoa, the transport of flagellar components is highly improbable, because IFT components disappear as spermatozoa mature (San Agustin et al., 2015).
evidence: Referenced to San Agustin et al., 2015.

claim: The distal and proximal region of zebrafish sperm could differ in the composition of axonemal dyneins.
source: Alternatively, the distal and proximal region of zebrafish sperm could differ in the composition of axonemal dyneins.
evidence: Proposed alternative explanation for proximal-distal differences.

claim: Human respiratory cilia have two types of OADs: DNAH11/DNAH5-containing OADs in the proximal and DNAH9/DNAH5-containing OADs in the distal parts.
source: Indeed, human respiratory cilia are known to have two types of OADs, that is DNAH11/DNAH5-containing OADs in the proximal and DNAH9/DNAH5-containing OADs in the distal parts (Figure 7E; Fliegauf et al., 2005; Dougherty et al., 2016).
evidence: Referenced to Fliegauf et al., 2005 and Dougherty et al., 2016.

claim: A mutation in the human KTU/DNAAF2 gene strongly affects the assembly of only distal OADs in respiratory cilia.
source: Intriguingly, a mutation in the human KTU/DNAAF2 gene strongly affects the assembly of only distal OADs in respiratory cilia (Omran et al., 2008).
evidence: Referenced to Omran et al., 2008.

claim: Testis showed the expression of two OAD γ-HC genes: dnah5 and dnah8.
source: Although testis showed the expression of two OAD γ-HC genes: dnah5 and dnah8, Dnah8 is present along the entire length of sperm flagella (Figure 4B) and the distribution of Dnah5 is not known.
evidence: Shown by in situ hybridization and immunofluorescence in Figure 4B and Figure 6A.

claim: Dnah8 is present along the entire length of sperm flagella.
source: Although testis showed the expression of two OAD γ-HC genes: dnah5 and dnah8, Dnah8 is present along the entire length of sperm flagella (Figure 4B) and the distribution of Dnah5 is not known.
evidence: Shown by immunofluorescence in Figure 4B.

claim: The distribution of Dnah5 in sperm flagella is not known.
source: Although testis showed the expression of two OAD γ-HC genes: dnah5 and dnah8, Dnah8 is present along the entire length of sperm flagella (Figure 4B) and the distribution of Dnah5 is not known.
evidence: Stated as unknown.

claim: Only dnah9 was detectable in testis as for OAD β-HC gene.
source: As for OAD β-HC gene, only dnah9 was detectable in testis (Figure 6).
evidence: Shown by in situ hybridization in Figure 6.

claim: In sperm flagella, Dnah9/Dnah8-containing OADs could be majority.
source: In sperm flagella, Dnah9/Dnah8-containing OADs could be majority as discussed above, while in Kupffer's vesicle cilia, the axonemes seem to be constituted of Dnah9/Dnah5-containing OADs and/or Dnah11/Dnah5-containing OADs (Figure 7D).
evidence: Inferred from DNAH gene expression patterns shown in Figure 7D.

claim: In Kupffer's vesicle cilia, the axonemes seem to be constituted of Dnah9/Dnah5-containing OADs and/or Dnah11/Dnah5-containing OADs.
source: In sperm flagella, Dnah9/Dnah8-containing OADs could be majority as discussed above, while in Kupffer's vesicle cilia, the axonemes seem to be constituted of Dnah9/Dnah5-containing OADs and/or Dnah11/Dnah5-containing OADs (Figure 7D).
evidence: Inferred from DNAH gene expression patterns shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The dynein compositions may vary depending on the pattern of ciliary beating.
source: It is tempting to speculate that the dynein compositions vary depending on the pattern of ciliary beating, as cilia and flagella of the two organs exhibit the different mode of movement, planar oscillation for sperm flagella and rotation for Kupffer's vesicle cilia.
evidence: Speculated based on correlation between dynein composition and beating patterns.

claim: Cilia and flagella of sperm and Kupffer's vesicle exhibit different modes of movement: planar oscillation for sperm flagella and rotation for Kupffer's vesicle cilia.
source: It is tempting to speculate that the dynein compositions vary depending on the pattern of ciliary beating, as cilia and flagella of the two organs exhibit the different mode of movement, planar oscillation for sperm flagella and rotation for Kupffer's vesicle cilia.
evidence: Observed from motility analyses.

claim: This is the first application of cryo-electron tomography to zebrafish sperm.
source: We applied cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) for the first time to zebrafish sperm, which enabled us to observe the detailed structure of wild-type and mutant axonemal dyneins.
evidence: Stated as a novel methodological application.

claim: Motile cilia/flagella are hair-like organelles that project from various types of eukaryotic cells.
source: Motile cilia/flagella are hair-like organelles that project from various types of eukaryotic cells.
evidence: Established knowledge about cilia/flagella.

claim: In humans, malfunctions of motile cilia often cause primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD).
source: In humans, malfunctions of motile cilia often cause primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), a syndrome characterized by recurrent respiratory infections, male infertility, hydrocephalus, and inversion of visceral laterality (Knowles et al., 2013; Brown and Witman, 2014).
evidence: Referenced to Knowles et al., 2013 and Brown and Witman, 2014.

claim: PCD is characterized by recurrent respiratory infections, male infertility, hydrocephalus, and inversion of visceral laterality.
source: In humans, malfunctions of motile cilia often cause primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), a syndrome characterized by recurrent respiratory infections, male infertility, hydrocephalus, and inversion of visceral laterality (Knowles et al., 2013; Brown and Witman, 2014).
evidence: Referenced to Knowles et al., 2013 and Brown and Witman, 2014.

claim: Motile cilia have a microtubule-based structure called an axoneme, consisting of nine peripheral doublet microtubules (DMTs) with or without central-pair microtubules (9 + 2, 9 + 0).
source: Motile cilia have a microtubule-based structure called an axoneme, consisting of nine peripheral doublet microtubules (DMTs) with or without central-pair microtubules (so called 9 + 2, 9 + 0, respectively).
evidence: Established knowledge about axoneme structure.

claim: Ciliary motility is driven by axonemal dyneins, which have multiple subtypes such as outer arm dyneins (OADs) and seven different types of inner arm dyneins (IADs; IAD a to g).
source: Ciliary motility is driven by axonemal dyneins, which have multiple subtypes such as outer arm dyneins (OADs) and seven different types of inner arm dyneins (IADs; IAD a to g; Kagami and Kamiya, 1992).
evidence: Referenced to Kagami and Kamiya, 1992.

claim: OAD is composed of three heavy chains (α-, β-, and γ-HC), two intermediate chains (IC1 and IC2), and ten light chains in Chlamydomonas.
source: Biochemical analyses of green algae Chlamydomonas revealed that each axonemal dynein consists of multiple subunits (Hom et al., 2011; Sakato and King, 2004); OAD is composed of three heavy chains (α-, β-, and γ-HC), two intermediate chains (IC1 and IC2), and ten light chains.
evidence: Referenced to Hom et al., 2011 and Sakato and King, 2004.

claim: Six types of IADs (IAD a, b, c, d, e, and g) have single HCs with several light chains such as p28, centrin, and actin in Chlamydomonas.
source: Six types of IADs (IAD a, b, c, d, e, and g) have single HCs with several light chains such as p28, centrin, and actin.
evidence: Established knowledge from Chlamydomonas studies.

claim: IAD f has two heavy chains (f α- and f β-HC), four intermediate chains, and five light chains in Chlamydomonas.
source: IAD f has two heavy chains (f α- and f β-HC), four intermediate chains, and five light chains.
evidence: Established knowledge from Chlamydomonas studies.

claim: Axonemal dyneins and all other large ciliary molecules are synthesized in the cytoplasm and undergo gated entry into the ciliary compartment.
source: In the process of ciliary construction, axonemal dyneins and all other large ciliary molecules are synthesized in the cytoplasm and undergo gated entry into the ciliary compartment (Takao and Verhey, 2016).
evidence: Referenced to Takao and Verhey, 2016.

claim: In the cytoplasm, the components of OADs and IADs are detected as preassembled complexes, rather than individual components.
source: In the cytoplasm, the components of OADs and IADs are detected as preassembled complexes, rather than individual components (Fok et al., 1994; Fowkes and Mitchell, 1998; Viswanadha et al., 2014).
evidence: Referenced to Fok et al., 1994; Fowkes and Mitchell, 1998; and Viswanadha et al., 2014.

claim: Cytoplasmic preassembly of axonemal dyneins requires various proteins collectively called dynein axonemal assembly factors (DNAAFs).
source: This cytoplasmic preassembly of axonemal dyneins requires various proteins collectively called dynein axonemal assembly factors (DNAAFs; Kobayashi and Takeda, 2012; Mitchison et al., 2012).
evidence: Referenced to Kobayashi and Takeda, 2012 and Mitchison et al., 2012.

claim: Cilia/flagella require multiple types of axonemal dyneins for their motions.
source: As cilia/flagella require multiple types of axonemal dyneins for their motions (Kamiya, 1995), proper assembly of each dynein complex is essential for ciliary motility.
evidence: Referenced to Kamiya, 1995.

claim: Proper assembly of each dynein complex is essential for ciliary motility.
source: As cilia/flagella require multiple types of axonemal dyneins for their motions (Kamiya, 1995), proper assembly of each dynein complex is essential for ciliary motility.
evidence: Logical inference from the requirement of multiple dyneins.

claim: The assembly processes of each dynein subtype and their roles in cilia/flagella motions remain elusive in vertebrates.
source: However, the assembly processes of each dynein subtype and their roles in cilia/flagella motions remain elusive in vertebrates.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap motivating the study.

claim: The PIH protein, which contains a PIH1-domain, was first identified in budding yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) as an interactor of HSP90 and named as Pih1.
source: The PIH protein, which contains a PIH1-domain, was first identified in budding yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) as an interactor of HSP90 and named as Pih1 (Protein Interacting with HSP90; also known as Nop17; Zhao et al., 2005; Gonzales et al., 2005).
evidence: Referenced to Zhao et al., 2005 and Gonzales et al., 2005.

claim: Yeast Pih1 is required for the assembly of various multi-subunit protein complexes but is not involved in the assembly of axonemal dyneins, as yeast do not have a cilium.
source: Yeast Pih1 is required for the assembly of various multi-subunit protein complexes but is not involved in the assembly of axonemal dyneins, as yeast do not have a cilium.
evidence: Established knowledge about yeast Pih1.

claim: In vertebrates, there are four PIH proteins: PIH1D1, PIH1D2, KTU/DNAAF2, and PIH1D3/TWISTER.
source: In vertebrates, there are four PIH proteins: PIH1D1, PIH1D2, KTU/DNAAF2, and PIH1D3/TWISTER, and PIH1D1 is the orthologue of yeast Pih1.
evidence: Established knowledge about vertebrate PIH proteins.

claim: PIH1D1 is the orthologue of yeast Pih1.
source: In vertebrates, there are four PIH proteins: PIH1D1, PIH1D2, KTU/DNAAF2, and PIH1D3/TWISTER, and PIH1D1 is the orthologue of yeast Pih1.
evidence: Established knowledge about PIH1D1.

claim: Human PIH1D1 is a subunit of the R2TP complex (RUVBL1, RUVBL2, RPAP3/Tah1, and PIH1D1), which interacts with HSP90 to promote assembly of various protein complexes.
source: Similar to yeast, the human PIH1D1 is a subunit of the R2TP complex (RUVBL1, RUVBL2, RPAP3/Tah1, and PIH1D1), which interacts with HSP90 to promote assembly of various protein complexes for cellular activities such as box C/D snoRNP and RNA polymerase II (Kakihara and Houry, 2012).
evidence: Referenced to Kakihara and Houry, 2012.

claim: KTU/DNAAF2 is the first protein that was identified as a DNAAF.
source: KTU/DNAAF2 is the first protein that was identified as a DNAAF (Omran et al., 2008).
evidence: Referenced to Omran et al., 2008.

claim: Genetic and biochemical analyses of KTU/DNAAF2 in medaka, human, and Chlamydomonas revealed that KTU/DNAAF2 is required for the assembly of OAD and a subset of IADs.
source: Genetic and biochemical analyses of KTU/DNAAF2 in medaka (Japanese killifish), human, and Chlamydomonas revealed that KTU/DNAAF2 is required for the assembly of OAD and a subset of IADs (Omran et al., 2008).
evidence: Referenced to Omran et al., 2008.

claim: Chlamydomonas MOT48 is a possible orthologue of vertebrate PIH1D1.
source: Subsequently, the function of Chlamydomonas MOT48, a possible orthologue of vertebrate PIH1D1, was reported; MOT48 is one of three PIH proteins in Chlamydomonas (MOT48, PF13/KTU, and TWI1) and is involved in the assembly of another subset of IDAs (Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: Referenced to Yamamoto et al., 2010.

claim: Chlamydomonas has three PIH proteins: MOT48, PF13/KTU, and TWI1.
source: Subsequently, the function of Chlamydomonas MOT48, a possible orthologue of vertebrate PIH1D1, was reported; MOT48 is one of three PIH proteins in Chlamydomonas (MOT48, PF13/KTU, and TWI1) and is involved in the assembly of another subset of IDAs (Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: Referenced to Yamamoto et al., 2010.

claim: Chlamydomonas MOT48 is involved in the assembly of a subset of IDAs.
source: Subsequently, the function of Chlamydomonas MOT48, a possible orthologue of vertebrate PIH1D1, was reported; MOT48 is one of three PIH proteins in Chlamydomonas (MOT48, PF13/KTU, and TWI1) and is involved in the assembly of another subset of IDAs (Yamamoto et al., 2010).
evidence: Referenced to Yamamoto et al., 2010.

claim: Pioneering studies proposed that preassembly of different subsets of axonemal dyneins is mediated by distinct PIH proteins.
source: These pioneering studies proposed that preassembly of different subsets of axonemal dyneins is mediated by distinct PIH proteins.
evidence: Summarizing previous studies on PIH proteins.

claim: Evidence for the hypothesis that preassembly of different subsets of axonemal dyneins is mediated by distinct PIH proteins is sparse, due to a lack of systematic studies of all PIH proteins.
source: However, evidence for this hypothesis is sparse, due to a lack of systematic studies of all PIH proteins.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap motivating the study.

claim: PIH1D3/TWISTER recently turned out to be one of the DNAAFs.
source: Although PIH1D3/TWISTER recently turned out to be one of the DNAAFs (Dong et al., 2014; Paff et al., 2017; Olcese et al., 2017), the function of vertebrate PIH1D1 and PIH1D2 has not been addressed in terms of ciliogenesis and ciliary motility.
evidence: Referenced to Dong et al., 2014; Paff et al., 2017; and Olcese et al., 2017.

claim: The function of vertebrate PIH1D1 and PIH1D2 has not been addressed in terms of ciliogenesis and ciliary motility.
source: Although PIH1D3/TWISTER recently turned out to be one of the DNAAFs (Dong et al., 2014; Paff et al., 2017; Olcese et al., 2017), the function of vertebrate PIH1D1 and PIH1D2 has not been addressed in terms of ciliogenesis and ciliary motility.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap motivating the study.

claim: Two Pih1d3 paralogues in mice, Pih1d3 and Twister2, are differently expressed in ciliary/flagellar organs (Pih1d3 for testis, while Twister2 for both testis and the others), suggesting a divergence of their functions.
source: Furthermore, two Pih1d3 paralogues in mice, Pih1d3 and Twister2, are differently expressed in ciliary/flagellar organs (Pih1d3 for testis, while Twister2 for both testis and the others; Dong et al., 2014), suggesting a divergence of their functions.
evidence: Referenced to Dong et al., 2014.
